title: EPIC: Research and foundation selection
objective: Select a supportable composition/fork strategy using pinned source, tests and licence evidence.
background: The project is in bootstrap and has no verified source audit.
approach: Complete core audits, compare candidates, record ADR and review trigger.
scope: OpenClaw, memory candidates, adapters and legal constraints.
out: Implement product services or select based only on README claims.
criteria: Pinned evidence for each core candidate; scored criteria with unknowns explicit; accepted ADR approved by maintainers.
tests: Research reproducibility and citation checks.

title: EPIC: Shared memory infrastructure
objective: Deliver scoped, provenance-bearing memory usable across authorised clients.
background: Portable memory is the durable product core.
approach: Structured versioned records, evidence, permission-first retrieval.
criteria: M1 memory scenarios and permission/provenance cases pass.
tests: Schema, migration, access-control, retrieval and deletion tests.

title: EPIC: CLI session integration
objective: Connect existing coding CLIs to shared context without requiring tool replacement.
background: Initial workflow is Claude Code ↔ Codex CLI.
approach: Documented versioned integration surfaces and idempotent adapters.
out: Undocumented transcript scraping or hidden reasoning transfer.
criteria: Bidirectional handover acceptance scenarios pass.
tests: Adapter contract tests against supported client versions.

title: EPIC: Incremental synchronisation
objective: Deliver durable replayable per-client event synchronization.
background: Returning clients need only unseen updates and bounded snapshots.
approach: Per-stream committed sequence, idempotent event IDs and durable acknowledgements.
scope: Ingest, cursors, replay, snapshot and conflict semantics.
criteria: Duplicate, crash, replay, permission revocation and cursor expiry scenarios pass.
tests: Transactional failure-injection and concurrency tests.

title: EPIC: Agent forum and messaging
milestone: M2: Automatic sync and agent forum
objective: Enable asynchronous scoped agent communication with auditable delivery and resolution.
background: Agents need handovers, questions and reviews.
approach: Typed messages, authenticated identity, scoped ACL and thread state.
criteria: Messages persist, replay, authorize and remain untrusted input.
tests: ACL, impersonation, replay, delivery/read, and injection tests.

title: EPIC: Unified model gateway
milestone: M3: Unified chat and model gateway
objective: Offer replaceable multi-provider access and usage visibility.
background: Gateway is a long-term optional component.
approach: Evaluate LiteLLM and integrate supported interfaces.
scope: Provider registry, credentials, streaming, usage and limits.
out: Reimplement mature gateway features without evidence.
criteria: Two independent providers work without provider-specific memory assumptions.
tests: Provider contract, credential redaction, streaming and accounting tests.

title: EPIC: Frontend workspace
milestone: M3: Unified chat and model gateway
objective: Provide chat, memory inspection and agent activity views.
background: Users need transparent control over knowledge and context.
approach: React + TypeScript UI consuming stable APIs.
criteria: Responsive accessible UI supports search, provenance, edits and permission visibility.
tests: Component, accessibility and end-to-end flows.

title: EPIC: Autonomous orchestration
objective: Plan and coordinate approval-gated isolated workers.
background: Orchestration is explicitly later phase.
approach: Capability registry, DAG, isolated runtime, budgets and audit.
out: Unrestricted host execution or current-phase implementation.
criteria: Workers operate within declared permissions, budgets and approvals with replayable reports.
tests: Sandbox escape, approvals, budget and lifecycle tests.

title: EPIC: Security and reliability
objective: Protect private context and ensure recoverable operation.
background: System processes conversations, repositories and potentially credentials.
approach: Threat model, least privilege, observability, backup and deletion.
criteria: Threat mitigations and recovery/deletion scenarios verified before hosted use.
tests: Security, isolation, recovery and adversarial tests.

title: Audit OpenClaw gateway architecture
objective: Determine whether OpenClaw gateway seams can be composed with AI_Uni.
background: OpenClaw is a strong but unverified candidate.
approach: Pin commit; inspect entrypoints, gateway protocol, auth, sessions, plugins and tests.
scope: Gateway architecture source and test audit.
criteria: Commit-pinned module map and claims cited to source and tests; unknowns recorded.
tests: Verify cited tests exist and are relevant.

title: Audit OpenClaw session events and reconciliation
objective: Verify session event ordering, reconnect and reconciliation implementation.
background: Per-client event recovery is central to product fit.
approach: Inspect source and failure/reconnect tests at pinned SHA.
scope: Session store, event log, watch cursors and reconciliation.
out: Assume WebSocket sequence alone is durable cursor.
criteria: Document durability, ordering, replay, acknowledgement, tests and limitations with pinned links.
tests: Check referenced cases in upstream test suite.

title: Audit memory implementations
objective: Compare TAM, Letta, Mem0, OpenMemory and Graphiti memory semantics.
background: Memory must be scoped, versioned, evidenced and incrementally retrievable.
approach: Inspect schema, ingestion, retrieval, conflict, deletion, tests and deployments.
out: Adopt based on feature list alone.
criteria: Per-project evidence matrix covers provenance, scopes, versions, temporal data, tokens and deletion.
tests: Test citations verified.

title: Audit Claude Code integration options
objective: Identify supported Claude Code hooks and event/artifact access limitations.
background: M1 needs capture without assuming transcript access.
approach: Use official versioned docs and a small compatibility matrix.
scope: Hooks, MCP, SDK, session lifecycle and permissions.
criteria: Document supported lifecycle, payloads, delivery limits, consent, versions and manual fallback with official citations.
tests: When available, exercise a minimal non-destructive hook sample.

title: Audit Codex CLI and app-server
objective: Map supported Codex CLI/app-server integration and event surfaces.
background: Codex is the reciprocal initial client.
approach: Review official docs and pinned open-source code/protocol tests.
scope: CLI commands, app-server, MCP, permissions, resume and events.
out: Conflate hosted Codex and CLI capabilities.
criteria: Versioned capability matrix, event completeness, auth/approval semantics and fallback documented.
tests: Validate claims against docs/source tests.

title: Confirm upstream licences
objective: Determine licence and reuse constraints for every candidate.
background: Commercial reuse cannot be inferred from public visibility.
approach: Inspect pinned full licence/notices and dependency/assets conditions.
scope: 17 manifest repositories and intended usage categories.
out: Legal conclusions beyond evidence or reuse approval.
criteria: Table records exact revision, licence text, notices, distribution implications and unresolved counsel questions.
tests: Cross-check licence files at recorded SHA.

title: Select fork/composition strategy
objective: Make evidence-based foundation selection or retain composition with explicit gates.
background: Current ADR is provisional.
approach: Score compatibility, effort, licensing, security, quality, modularity, scale, cadence and DX.
scope: At least OpenClaw and two serious alternatives.
criteria: Decision includes pinned source/test evidence, alternatives, costs, risks, integration boundaries and review trigger; ADR accepted.
tests: Maintainer review of citations and criteria.

title: Define canonical event schema
objective: Define evolvable canonical event contract across CLI adapters.
background: Candidate fields exist in design docs but are not final.
approach: Specify identity, scope, sequence, timestamps, payload references, hashes and schema evolution.
criteria: Schema versioned; ordering/dedup/privacy semantics documented; examples cover session/file/decision/test/handover.
tests: Schema compatibility and validation fixtures.

title: Define scoped memory schema
objective: Specify scoped records and evidence lifecycle.
background: Avoid a single rewritten markdown knowledge file.
approach: Define scope, version, provenance, confidence, validity, conflict, permissions and deletion fields.
criteria: Schema examples and migration, review, contradiction, retention and cross-project rules documented.
tests: Model invariant test plan included.

title: Define sync cursor and acknowledgement protocol
objective: Specify safe incremental delivery and recovery.
background: A client cursor must not move ahead of durable apply.
approach: Specify per-client stream cursor, commit receipt, apply ack, expiry, snapshot and replay.
criteria: State transitions cover duplicate, lost response, crash, permission change, compaction and cursor revocation.
tests: Failure matrix turned into executable test cases.

title: Implement local event store
objective: Persist validated scoped events locally with idempotent ingest.
background: Required for reliable handover MVP.
approach: Use selected local-first database with transactional sequence allocation.
scope: Append, query, dedupe, replay and migration.
deps: Define sync cursor and acknowledgement protocol
criteria: Commit precedes receipt; duplicate key returns original event; replay preserves order and data.
tests: Crash/duplicate/concurrency/schema migration tests.

title: Design memory snapshot system
objective: Design bounded authoritative snapshots with high-watermarks and provenance.
background: Fresh clients need useful context without full history.
approach: Define selection, compaction, watermark, token budget and delta continuation.
deps: Define sync cursor and acknowledgement protocol
criteria: Snapshot declares coverage and versions; recovery after expiration cannot skip events; token budget measurable.
tests: Snapshot/delta boundary and stale snapshot scenarios specified.

title: Build Claude Code event adapter
objective: Publish supported Claude session events/artifact references into canonical store.
background: First direction of M1 workflow.
approach: Use verified supported hooks/API; idempotent outbox and manual command fallback.
scope: Capture authorized decisions, file references, test results and handover.
criteria: Adapter handles duplicate/lost receipt, records source/version, and documents unsupported data.
tests: Fixture and live compatibility tests under documented supported version.

title: Build Codex event adapter
objective: Publish supported Codex CLI/app-server events/artifacts into canonical store.
background: Reciprocal M1 client.
approach: Use verified official protocol/CLI surfaces; idempotent delivery.
scope: Decisions, changes, test outcomes and handover.
criteria: Adapter reports capabilities, retries safely and supports incremental context load.
tests: Protocol fixture and compatibility tests.

title: Implement manual synchronisation
objective: Allow user-triggered push/pull sync independent of automatic hooks.
background: Not all clients expose equivalent hooks.
approach: CLI commands expose preview, push, pull, status and explicit acknowledgement.
deps: Define sync cursor and acknowledgement protocol
criteria: Repeated sync is idempotent; preview shows scope; failures preserve cursor for retry.
tests: CLI contract and offline/retry tests.

title: Implement automatic session-end synchronisation
milestone: M2: Automatic sync and agent forum
objective: Trigger reliable synchronization at supported session lifecycle boundaries.
background: Automatic sync is a convenience over durable manual sync.
approach: Use verified hooks plus durable local outbox and reconciliation.
out: Assume hooks always run or are complete.
criteria: Hook failure/restart is recovered without loss; user can inspect and disable capture.
tests: Failure injection, duplicate callback, privacy and version tests.

title: Implement conflict detection
objective: Detect competing claims and preserve both with evidence.
background: Agents may make conflicting decisions or observations.
approach: Compare scoped versioned claims and create explicit conflict relations.
criteria: Conflicts cite sources, remain visible, and only an authorized resolution changes accepted view.
tests: Concurrent edits, stale claims and resolution authorization tests.

title: Implement provenance tracking
objective: Trace important memory claims to source events and artifacts.
background: Generated knowledge needs evidence and user review.
approach: Store source references and derivation metadata at claim level.
out: Treat inferred memory as user-confirmed fact.
criteria: Every promoted decision/requirement shows origin, actor, time and validation state.
tests: Missing, inaccessible and deleted-source behavior tests.

title: Implement agent messaging schema
milestone: M2: Automatic sync and agent forum
objective: Define typed thread/message/delivery/resolution records.
background: Asynchronous handovers require stable semantics.
approach: Scope messages, identity, source refs, related tasks and ack states.
out: Agent authority implied by message content.
criteria: Schema handles recipients/topics, replies, delivery/read, resolution, replay and revocation.
tests: Invariant and ACL cases specified.

title: Build forum service
milestone: M2: Automatic sync and agent forum
objective: Provide permission-scoped agent message and review operations.
background: Forum schema supports handovers and asynchronous collaboration.
approach: Persist messages transactionally with identity checks and notification outbox.
criteria: All operations enforce scope and produce auditable state transitions.
tests: ACL, replay, impersonation, injection and notification delivery tests.

title: Add memory inspection UI
milestone: M2: Automatic sync and agent forum
objective: Let users inspect, correct, dispute and delete stored knowledge.
background: Memory must remain user-governable.
approach: Build source-linked scoped explorer with pending updates and history.
criteria: User can view provenance, edit, resolve conflict, revoke and delete within permissions.
tests: Accessibility, authorization and deletion propagation e2e.

title: Integrate model gateway
milestone: M3: Unified chat and model gateway
objective: Integrate selected provider gateway without coupling memory to provider SDKs.
background: Gateway capabilities may be delegated to mature infrastructure.
approach: Use LiteLLM if audit verifies fit; document alternatives and credentials boundary.
scope: Provider config, model discovery, streaming and usage.
criteria: At least two providers route and stream through stable interface; secrets do not enter logs/events.
tests: Provider contract, error, rate-limit and redaction tests.

title: Implement unified chat
milestone: M3: Unified chat and model gateway
objective: Provide provider-selectable chat with project context and usage visibility.
background: Long-term UI is a consumer of shared memory, not its owner.
approach: React/TypeScript client over gateway and memory APIs.
scope: Chat history, streaming, project selection, attachments and usage.
criteria: User switches models while retaining permission-scoped conversation context and history.
tests: Streaming, access control, cost display and accessibility e2e.

title: Implement model capability registry
milestone: M3: Unified chat and model gateway
objective: Represent versioned provider/model capabilities for informed routing.
background: Future selection requires limits, modalities and measured behavior.
approach: Store capability source/time and distinguish advertised from measured values.
criteria: Capabilities include provenance, freshness, limits and explicit unknowns.
tests: Provider metadata drift and validation tests.

title: Implement orchestrator execution lifecycle
objective: Coordinate planned tasks, workers, approvals, budgets and final audit.
background: Autonomous orchestration is a future phase.
approach: Model lifecycle as auditable state machine over stable task/event contracts.
scope: Plan, dispatch, wait, review, approve and report.
criteria: Task states and transitions are replayable; sensitive actions wait for user approval.
tests: State-machine, timeout, cancellation, budget and approval tests.

title: Build isolated agent worker runtime
objective: Execute workers in scoped isolated environments.
background: Autonomous agents must not get unrestricted host access.
approach: Evaluate containers/worktrees and independent permission grants.
scope: Filesystem, process, network and secret boundaries.
criteria: Worker access is least privilege, observable, revocable and cleaned up after completion.
tests: Adversarial escape and permission matrix tests.

title: Define security and permissions model
objective: Specify actor, tenant, project and operation authorization rules.
background: Memory and tool execution cross sensitive boundaries.
approach: Threat-model read/write/execute/network/credential grants and revocation.
scope: Data access and future worker permissions.
out: Implicit trust based on model/provider identity.
criteria: Threats map to enforceable controls and test cases; deletion, revocation and approval policies documented.
tests: Security review of threat/control coverage.

title: Build end-to-end handover tests
objective: Automate Claude-to-Codex and Codex-to-Claude acceptance flows.
background: This is the defining MVP outcome.
approach: Use deterministic fixtures/client doubles, then supported live compatibility checks.
scope: Changed files, decisions, tests, unresolved tasks and provenance.
criteria: Both directions pass without copying context; incremental, fresh, conflict and recovery scenarios included.
tests: CI end-to-end suite with reproducible fixtures.

title: Implement observability
objective: Trace event delivery, sync lag and failures without exposing private payloads.
background: Reliable operation needs measurable delivery and recovery.
approach: Structured redacted metrics/logs with correlation IDs and retention bounds.
criteria: Operators can diagnose lag, retries and failures; sensitive payloads are excluded by tests.
tests: Redaction, cardinality and alert behavior tests.

title: Build documentation and onboarding
objective: Make local setup, concepts, contribution and troubleshooting reproducible.
background: Project must be understandable to contributors and coding agents.
approach: Keep quick start synchronized with tested commands and architecture links.
criteria: A new contributor follows docs to validate repo and find a ready Issue; all links/commands checked.
tests: Documentation link and clean-environment walkthrough.
